findings.title: Fallback chain built from SiteSetting at runtime; loaded fallback locales only ensured in controllers
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup. Fallback locales are only loaded by ensure_loaded!, and that is called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. In jobs, mailers, and rake tasks, I18n.translate loads only config.locale, so a missing key falls back to a locale that was never loaded and returns 'translation missing'. Load the fallback locales inside I18n.translate / load_locale instead of relying on the controller.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU cache key is key + locale + backend id. The fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, which can change at runtime or differ per site in multisite. A cached fallback result, or a cached 'missing' result computed before the fallback locale was loaded, keeps being served afterwards. Users can get stale or wrong-language strings until the cache is evicted.

findings.title: Hash subclass only overrides [] for fallbacks
findings.body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale], which works here. Other code (e.g. Rails' I18n railtie or gems) may call fetch, defaults=, or expect an I18n::Locale::Fallbacks instance. A plain Hash subclass returns nil or empty results from those calls, which can break lookups in subtle ways.
